title: The subclouds API: reading subclouds and editing their data center exclusions

prose.text: Subclouds are created by Zscaler, but a tenant can read them and edit their data center exclusions through the ZIA API. The endpoints themselves are in the generated surface (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface /subclouds`).

prose.label: Writing.
prose.text: {{put-exclusions}} {{put-id-is-subcloud}} The OpenAPI document describes that path ID differently {{divergence:put-path-id}}.

prose.label: Creating and deleting.
prose.text: {{no-create-in-contract}} {{creation-stays-with-support}} Whether a subcloud can be deleted through the API is disputed {{divergence:delete-route}}.

checks.do: To find a subcloud's name and its excluded data centers, read the subcloud list rather than asking Support.
When updating exclusions, put the subcloud's ID in the path, as both SDKs do.

list-with-exclusions.statement: GET /subclouds retrieves all of the organization's subclouds with the excluded data centers associated with each; each entry carries an ID, a name, its list of data centers and its exclusions.

expect.description: Retrieves all the subclouds and the excluded data centers that are associated with the subcloud
List of data centers that are excluded from the subcloud

exclusion-state.statement: Each exclusion names its data center and country, carries start, end, creation and last-modified times and the last modifying user, and two flags: `disabledByOps`, set when Zscaler CloudOps has disabled the exclusion, and `expired`, described as the exclusion being disabled.

expect.description: If set to true, this data center exclusion is disabled by Zscaler CloudOps
The subcloud data center exclusion is disabled

put-exclusions.statement: PUT /subclouds/{id} updates the subcloud and its excluded data centers; the request body is the organization's subcloud with its list of excluded data centers.

expect.description: Updates the subcloud and excluded data centers based on the specified ID
The organization's subcloud containing the list of excluded data centers

put-id-is-subcloud.statement: Go's `Update` formats its `cloudID` argument into the `/zia/api/v1/subclouds` path, and Python's `update_sub_clouds` takes `cloud_id`, documented as the unique ID for the Sub Clouds.

quotes: func Update(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, cloudID int, subClouds *SubClouds) (*SubClouds, *http.Response, error) {
cloud_id (int): The unique ID for the Sub Clouds.

no-create-in-contract.statement: The OpenAPI contract has no POST, PUT or DELETE on /subclouds and no GET, POST or DELETE on /subclouds/{id}.

creation-stays-with-support.statement: So creating a subcloud is not an API operation: it stays a Support request, and the API covers reading subclouds and editing their exclusions.
creation-stays-with-support.conditions: Rests on the absence of a create operation in the published contract; an undocumented route would change it.

put-path-id.summary: What the ID in PUT /subclouds/{id} identifies.

expect.description: Unique identifier for the excluded data center

positions.says: The OpenAPI document describes the path ID as the unique identifier for the excluded data center.

quotes: cloud_id (int): The unique ID for the Sub Clouds.

positions.says: The Python SDK (and the Go SDK's cloudID argument) treat it as the subcloud's ID.

put-path-id.impact: A caller following the OpenAPI wording would put a data center ID in the path and update the wrong subcloud or none.

positions.says: The OpenAPI contract lists no DELETE operation for a subcloud.
